h1: Rugged tablets for the Protean Software engineer app
intro: Protean Software is UK service management software for businesses that supply, install, maintain or hire equipment. Protean Software Ltd was based in Coventry until Joblogic acquired it in July 2023 and moved the team to Joblogic's Birmingham offices; the Protean product line continues under the Joblogic group, and the vendor site lists Protean FSM alongside Joblogic FSM. Its sectors page names catering equipment, CCTV, medical equipment, cleaning, electrical engineering, commercial vehicles, facilities management, fire safety, forklifts, gardening, gas engineering, lifts and elevators, pest control, plumbing, radio and telecommunications and tail lifts, and the home page carries testimonials from lift, compressed air, stairlift, cleaning, heating and cooling, electrical and CCTV firms.

The engineer-facing part is the mobile engineer application, which the vendor describes as available for iOS and Android devices. Engineers receive jobs allocated from a drag-and-drop planner board, are shown on a map with Google Maps directions, record extra work and the parts needed, identify parts by barcode reading, log time so timesheets are submitted automatically, dictate reports or use a phrasebook instead of typing, and capture customer signatures and on-site images so that signed job sheets can be emailed automatically. The home page states that engineers can complete jobs and capture signatures even when offline.

This page sets out what Protean publishes about device requirements, which Tuga devices meet those published figures, and what it does not publish. One caution up front: the vendor's technical specifications page is dated 20 November 2016, and the engineer app could not be found on Google Play under the Protean name when we looked on 25 October 2026, so confirm with Protean or Joblogic support which app and version your contract covers before you buy devices for it.

requirements.detail: Protean's knowledge base article What are the technical specifications?, dated 20 November 2016, lists mobile devices as Android 4.4 or later only; the page does not mention iOS, although the current home page says the engineer app is available for iOS and Android devices. Android 4.4 is a 2013 release, so every current Android device clears it; the open question is which Android versions the current build of the app actually supports, which the vendor does not publish. Ask Protean or Joblogic support before relying on this figure.

The same 2016 specification requires a rear-facing camera. The mobile engineer application page describes capturing on-site images and identifying parts by barcode reading, and the home page describes capturing signatures, so the camera is used for photographs and, most likely, for reading barcodes; the vendor does not say whether a dedicated scan engine is supported.

The 2016 specification requires a 3G or 4G data plan on the mobile device, which rules out a Wi-Fi only tablet. The app communicates with Protean's web services over HTTPS on port 443, which the specification says must be reachable from the internet, so the device needs its own mobile data for jobs to update between sites.

requirements.requirement: 16GB or more storage, from a reputable brand
requirements.detail: The 2016 specification asks for 16GB or more of storage and a device from a reputable brand. The small business server option notes that disk needs grow if engineers upload photos, which is a reminder that photographs are what fill a device too.

The home page states that engineers can complete jobs and capture signatures even when offline. The specification does not describe how much data is held on the device or how sync is handled, so test a full job offline on a trial unit before relying on it in a plant room or a lift shaft with no signal.

requirements.requirement: Desktop client: Windows 8, 8.1 or 10 Professional or Enterprise
requirements.detail: The 2016 specification says the desktop client runs on Windows 8 and 8.1 and on Windows 10 Professional and Enterprise, is built on 32-bit Microsoft Access Runtime 2010 or 2016, cannot be installed alongside 64-bit Office, and needs a wired network connection to the SQL Server; remote users work through a full remote desktop session. Windows 11 is not listed. This is the office product, not the engineer app.

recommended.why: The Tuga A10 is the pick for engineers who work from job sheets, equipment histories and attached manuals. It runs Android 14, well above the published Android 4.4 floor, with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage against the 16GB minimum, and its 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen gives a full job sheet, a checklist and a signature box room without scrolling. Dual SIM 4G meets the 3G or 4G data plan requirement, and the 13MP rear camera with flash covers on-site images and camera-based barcode reading in a dim plant room or lift motor room. It is sealed to IP68 and tested to MIL-STD-810H, and it works from -20C to 60C. The trade-offs are a 350 nit screen, which is readable under cover but not the brightest in the range, and a battery that is not removable.

recommended.why: The Tuga A8 (£379) suits engineers who spend the day in and out of a van and want the tablet docked between jobs. It runs Android 12 with Google Play, has 6GB RAM and 128GB storage, and its 8 inch screen is rated at 1000 nits, which helps when a job sheet is filled in outside or in a bright yard. The 8000mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over on a long day, and VESA mount points with a pogo pin connector let it lock into the Vehicle Mounting Dock. Against the A10, which costs £70 more, it is IP67 rather than IP68, lists no MIL-STD rating or operating temperature, runs an older Android release and has a lower 1280 x 800 resolution, so a dense job sheet needs more scrolling.
fit: Android 4.4 or later: Android 12 on a MediaTek Helio P35 octa-core up to 2.3GHz, 6GB RAM, 128GB storage and a microSD slot.
Rear-facing camera: 13MP autofocus rear camera with flash and a 5MP front camera.
3G or 4G data plan: 4G LTE with dual SIM, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

Van-based days: IP67, removable 8000mAh battery, VESA mount points, pogo pin dock connector, USB-C and DC in, 1000 nit screen under AGC glass.

recommended.why: Where an engineer wants a device that lives in a pocket or a belt holster rather than a tablet under the arm, the Tuga A6 (£349) runs Android 15 on a 6 inch handheld at 277g, with dual SIM 4G for the data plan requirement, a 13MP rear camera with flash, IP67 sealing and a 1.5 metre drop rating. It also carries a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, which is relevant to Protean's parts barcode reading if the app accepts keyboard-wedge input; the vendor does not document that, so test it. The trade-offs are the 6 inch screen, which makes a long job sheet and a signature box cramped, and 4GB RAM with 64GB storage (microSD up to 256GB), which clears the 16GB minimum but leaves less room for photographs and manuals than the tablets.

not_recommended_note: The Tuga W10 and W8 are not recommended for Protean on the strength of what the vendor publishes. The engineer app is published for Android (and, per the home page, iOS), not Windows. The office desktop client is listed for Windows 8, 8.1 and 10 Professional or Enterprise on 32-bit Access Runtime with a wired connection to the SQL Server; the W10 and W8 run Windows 11 Pro, which the 2016 specification does not list, and a tablet is not the right shape for a 32-bit Access front end in any case. If Joblogic confirms the current desktop client on Windows 11, the W10's RJ45 Ethernet port meets the wired network requirement, but ask first. Two further cautions. The technical specifications page is dated 20 November 2016 and no newer requirement has been published, so treat Android 4.4 as a historical floor rather than a statement about today's app. And the engineer app could not be found on Google Play under the Protean or Joblogic names when we looked on 25 October 2026, which suggests it is supplied by the vendor rather than from the public store; ask support (02476 710300, option 2, or support.proteansoftware.com) how it is installed before buying devices. Nothing on this page is a vendor recommendation, and no Tuga device has been tested or certified by Protean Software Ltd or Joblogic.
setup_steps: Confirm with Protean or Joblogic support (02476 710300, option 2, or the support portal at support.proteansoftware.com) which engineer app and version your contract covers, which Android versions it currently supports, and how it is distributed, since it was not found on Google Play under the vendor's name.

Ask your IT administrator to confirm the Protean web services are reachable from the internet over HTTPS on port 443 with a static hostname and SSL certificate, as the vendor's specification requires; the app cannot sync without that.
Install the app on the Tuga A10, A8 or A6 as the vendor directs, sign in with the engineer credentials your administrator issues, and grant the camera, location and storage permissions it asks for.
Insert a SIM with a data plan (the A10, A8 and A6 all take two) so jobs, parts and signatures update between sites; the specification requires 3G or 4G data rather than Wi-Fi alone.

Before the first real job, put the device in flight mode and complete a test job with a signature and a photograph to confirm the offline behaviour the vendor describes, then reconnect and check it arrives in the office.

Fit the Vehicle Mounting Dock in the van for the A8 or A10, or the Belt Holster for the A6, add a tempered glass screen protector, and register the device's 12-month warranty at tugahardware.com/register-warranty.

faq.q: Will the Protean engineer app run on the Tuga A10?
faq.a: Protean's published mobile requirement is Android 4.4 or later with a rear-facing camera, 16GB or more of storage and a 3G or 4G data plan, from a specification dated 20 November 2016. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with 128GB of storage, a 13MP rear camera and dual SIM 4G, so it meets every published figure. We do not claim the A10 has been tested or certified by Protean Software Ltd or Joblogic, and because the specification is from 2016 we recommend confirming the current app's supported Android versions with the vendor and trialling one unit before a fleet order.

faq.q: Why can we not find the Protean app on Google Play?
faq.a: When we looked on 25 October 2026, no app from Protean Software Ltd or Joblogic carrying the Protean name was listed on Google Play; the proteän and Protean Connect apps that appear in searches belong to unrelated companies. The vendor describes the engineer app as available for iOS and Android, so it is most likely distributed by Protean directly or through your administrator. Ask support how your engineers install it, and whether a Joblogic app is now used instead; our Joblogic page covers that app's published requirements.

Protean's home page states that engineers can complete jobs and capture signatures even when offline. The vendor does not publish how much job data is held on the device or how sync works afterwards, so test a full job in flight mode on a trial unit. The A10, A8 and A6 all take a SIM, which meets the published 3G or 4G data plan requirement for syncing between sites.

faq.q: Is there a Windows tablet option for Protean?
faq.a: Not one we can recommend from what the vendor publishes. The engineer app is published for Android and iOS, and the office desktop client is listed for Windows 8, 8.1 and 10 Professional or Enterprise on a 32-bit Access Runtime with a wired network connection to the SQL Server. The Tuga W10 and W8 run Windows 11 Pro, which is not on that list. If Joblogic confirms the current desktop client on Windows 11, the W10 has an RJ45 Ethernet port for the wired connection, but confirm before buying.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. Order a single unit and try it with your Protean login before the rest; if it is wrong, return it within 30 days in its original condition, box and all. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice. Tuga Hardware is the trading name of Destello Tech Ltd and is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the listed prices. Delivery is free to UK addresses in 7 to 10 working days, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty. Team discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 devices, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more.
